svg.title: Asking an AI versus measuring it: visibility distance of a dark spot
svg.desc: Told the size and contrast, Claude Opus 5.5 lands a typical 1.3x from the model's average-observer distance, but identical asks spread by 27% (median CV), and doubling the spot raised its answer by 1.4x to 2.3x, not 2.0x. 23 of 45 answers fall inside the model's range. Per-patch values are in summary.json.
svg.text: Why not just ask an AI?
Told the size and contrast, Claude Opus 5.5 lands a typical 1.3x from the model's average-observer distance,
but identical asks spread by 27% (median CV), and doubling the spot raised its answer by 1.4x to 2.3x, not 2.0x.
Claude Opus 5.5 on Amazon Bedrock: each of its 5 answers per patch
Our model: average observer (left end) to one-sided bound (right end)
1. How far away can the dark spot on a 60 mm skin patch still be seen?
Asked with the spot's size and contrast stated, for 20/20 vision in indoor light.
Spot 5% darker than the surrounding skin

svg.text: Farthest distance at which the spot can still be seen (log scale: each gridline doubles it)
2. Does doubling the spot double the distance?
Ratio of the median answers. At fixed contrast, distance scales with size, so the ideal is 2.0.
Grey whisker: lowest to highest ratio over all 25 pairs of one answer per size.
Ideal 2.0: our model gives 2.00 for every pair

svg.text: Distance after doubling the spot's diameter, divided by the distance before (log scale)
Model: Watson & Ahumada (2005) Standard A, validated on ModelFest observers (0.69 dB RMS), at 45 cd/m2 for 20/20 vision.
Bound = the same model made 6 dB more sensitive (a sharper-than-average eye). Distances are not capped at 10 m here.
Raw answers and prompts: eval/llm-baseline/. 65 calls, 116945 tokens, about $1.11 at list price.
